summary: Permission shadowing during ephemeral SA provisioning blocks LLM debugger from accessing KMS-wrapped artifacts in prod
description: Issue summary: Ephemeral service account created by the provisioning broker for the LLM debugger in prod is missing the necessary Cloud KMS decrypt binding, causing model artifact access failures.
impact: Critical: On-call SREs cannot attach the debugger to live inference pods in prod. Debug sessions fail with KMS access denied which prevents investigation of a P0 latency spike. Potential customer impact if a rollback or hotfix is required and cannot be validated.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger ephemeral SA provisioning via infra-provisioner (flow: /provision/debugger-session) for project redwood-prod-llm.
2) Attempt to start debugger VM container that reads model artifact from GCS encrypted with KMS key projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/llm/cryptoKeys/model-key.
3) Observe KMS API call failures (cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt) with AccessDenied errors in the debugger logs and KMS audit logs.
4) Compare bindings for the ephemeral SA in staging vs prod: staging SA includes roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter; prod SA does not.
observed_behavior: Debugger container logs show: "google.api_core.exceptions.PermissionDenied: 403 Permission denied for cloudkms.cryptoKeys.decrypt". IAM audit shows the ephemeral SA is created but the roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter binding is missing. Provisioner audit trail indicates a conditional role attachment was evaluated and skipped in the prod project.
expected_behavior: Ephemeral service account should receive a minimal set of critical bindings including roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter and roles/storage.objectViewer so debugger can read and decrypt model artifacts in prod.
logs: debugger/container.log: 2026-03-10T14:02:21Z ERROR KMS decrypt failed: PermissionDenied
iam/audit.log: 2026-03-10T13:59:18Z WARN conditional-binding-eval: predicate 'env=="staging"' evaluated false; skipped roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Ava): Observed consistent repro in prod only; staging provisioning works as expected.

SRE (Ravi): Looked at provisioner code path and found a recent change that attempts to 'shadow' environment-specific roles by checking the 'env' attribute on the request and applying a different binding set if tag != 'prod'.

Found in provisioner logs: the env tag attached to the provisioning request is being normalized by the org-attribute-mapper which strips long env names. In ~3% of requests in prod the env tag is dropped which triggers the fallback role set (which omits KMS decrypt).

GCP OrgPolicy/Constraint review: No explicit deny on cloudkms.decrypt, but there is a conditional policy applied at folder level that only allows 'roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter' when the SA principal has attribute 'env:prod' attached. If attribute missing, binding is not permitted by the guardrail enforcement script.
Cross-check: We reproduced by creating an ephemeral SA with missing 'env' attribute and observed the same denial and missing binding.
hypotheses: 1) Provisioner attribute normalization bug: env tag is truncated/omitted for some long-lived provisioning tokens causing role attachment to fall to fallback set.
2) New guardrail enforcement introduced last week rejects binding attachments that don't include the env attribute; provisioner did not account for this change.
3) Race between attribute-sync service and provisioner: SA is created before attributes are written, enforcement denies conditional binding at attach time.
actions_taken: 2026-03-10 15:30 UTC: Temporarily applied a scoped, timebound binding roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to sa-debugger-ephem-* in redwood-prod-llm by ops-runbook with justification 'emergency debug'.
2026-03-10 16:05 UTC: Added a monitoring alert on provisioning events where 'env' attribute is missing for prod requests.
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC: Provisioner team deployed a hotfix to rehydrate missing env attribute before role-attachment step (canary to 5% of provisioning flows).
2026-03-11 12:00 UTC: SRE validated that newly provisioned ephemeral SAs in canary now receive KMS binding and debugger attach succeeded in 3 test sessions.
2026-03-12 08:00 UTC: Ops revoked emergency scoped bindings after canary validated and hotfix promoted.
next_steps: 1) Expand canary rollout to 100% after another 24h stable metrics (provisioner team).
2) Add unit + e2e test in provisioner pipeline that asserts required critical bindings are present for prod provisioning flows.
3) Update org-attribute-mapper to emit a non-fatal warning and retry logic if attributes are not persisted within 10s.
4) Security to review conditional policy scopes and document minimal explicit allow list for critical service flows.
5) Run a retrospective to decide whether to relax the attribute requirement for emergency ops flows or add a bypass with strict audit logging.
resolution: (in progress) Hotfix deployed and emergency bindings applied then revoked. Canaries show binding correctness. Waiting on full rollout and additional test coverage before marking resolved.
